subject: general
question: At which position on principal axis does a concave mirror forms a highly diminished, real and inverted image of an object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**beyond 2F**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed **beyond 2F (center of curvature)** of a concave mirror, the image formed is **real, inverted, and highly diminished**.
 
• The image is formed **between F and 2F** on the same side of the mirror.
 
• The farther the object from the mirror, the **smaller and closer the image moves towards the focus (F)**.
 
• If the object is placed at infinity, the image is **point-sized at the focal point**.
 
• This is a standard behavior of concave mirrors according to ray diagram principles in optics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror Image Characteristics:**

 
 
• **Beyond 2F**: Real, inverted, diminished (image forms between F and 2F).
 
• **At 2F**: Real, inverted, same size (image forms at 2F).
 
• **Between F and 2F**: Real, inverted, enlarged (image forms beyond 2F).
 
• **At F**: Image at infinity.
 
• **Between Pole and F**: Virtual, erect, enlarged (image forms behind the mirror).
 
 
 
• **Ray Diagram Rules:**
 
 
• Ray parallel to principal axis reflects through the focus.
 
• Ray through the center reflects back along the same path.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is focal length, v is image distance, and u is object distance.
 
• Used to calculate exact image location and characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• All distances measured from mirror's pole.
 
• Distances in the direction of incoming light are negative (object side), and in the direction of reflected light are positive.
 
 
 
• **Use of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used in telescopes, headlights, shaving mirrors, and solar concentrators due to their ability to focus light.
